items: Last year a quota bump on a finance mailbox let a billing error pile up unnoticed for weeks, so I like the data owner to actually sign off before finance-side capacity grows.
Finance operations has passed along 'the CFO approved it' to me before when the CFO had only been cc'd on a thread, so a relayed approval is not the same as a confirmed one for me.
A bigger finance mailbox means more sensitive financial material retained in one place, so I treat capacity increases there as a decision with a real owner, not a routine setting.

Finance runs a standing month-end close capacity cycle, and the CFO pre-clears the temporary quota bumps for it with me at the start of each quarter, so finance operations relaying that schedule is reliable.
When finance-ops is handling the close, a 10 GB working ceiling is the agreed size we use; it is on the close runbook the CFO signed.
Capacity for the close window is squarely my call to action once the close calendar names it, and finance operations is the team I take that schedule from.
